So, while the goalie has a specific role, other players also have roles in defending and preventing the opposing team from scoring. So, maybe expecting the goalie alone to stop the ball isn't the right approach. It should be a collective effort. Another thing to consider is the pressure on the goalie. It's important to support each other as a team rather than putting all the pressure on one person. On the other hand, if the goalie is part of the team and has agreed to take on that responsibility, then it's their duty to try their best to stop the ball. So, in that sense, expecting them to do their job is reasonable. But it's also important to have realistic expectations and understand that no one can win every game or stop every shot. I'm also thinking about the concept of accountability. If the goalie fails to stop the ball, is it solely their fault, or is it a team issue? Probably a bit of both.
